cli_version.description: The release the launching CLI ran as (task.Spec.CLIVersion, D3441): the runner compares it with its own and, when the stamp is newer, upgrades in place to exactly that release before it runs the task. Absent for every spec written before this field and for every launch from a development build, which has no release tag to fetch and stamps nothing (D3449): absent means no stamp, and the release the image already holds runs. The pattern is task.releaseVersionRE, the shape updatecheck.Valid carries: a strict X.Y.Z with an optional 'v', no pre-release or build suffix. A task that carries one needs a runner that reads the field, since task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields; that is D3445's launch window, accepted rather than gated at launch (D3448).

base_branch.description: The base the launcher resolved from the layers below the repository's own file (config.EffectiveBaseBranch: the local config's repos.<r>.base_branch, else the project's base_branch, which a machine whose own config sets none reads from the published policy node). The runner uses it only when the fugaro.yaml at the ref does not set git.base_branch itself, which is the first layer. Absent (omitempty) for a launch whose file names the base, and for one whose resolved value is main, which is the fallback the file's own resolution already has; the launcher's skew gate omits it against a job image older than 0.12.1 rather than refusing the launch. The rules here are config.ValidBranchName's, the one validator fugaro.yaml's git.base_branch, the installation config's own top-level base_branch and the policy node's are all held to: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/', not starting with '-', '.' or '/', with no '..', '//', component starting with '.', or trailing '/', '.' or '.lock'.

title.description: The run's own job title (fugaro run --title, task.Spec.Title): the one line every surface that names the run shows (task.TitleLine). Absent for every launch that gave none, which is where the title is the task prompt's own first line. It is refused unless it is one non-empty line of at most 100 runes with no control character (task.TitleProblem, applied by the launcher and by task.Parse), which is what the pattern and maxLength here carry apart from the whitespace-only case. Needs a 0.8.5 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's titlesSince): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it. This property was missing until the console dependency graph's GV1.2 added its sibling: schemas/task.schema.json is additionalProperties: false, so every launch with --title wrote a task.json this schema rejected.

plan_task.description: The plan task this run works on (fugaro run --plan-task; console dependency graph plan GV1.2, decision GD5): <plan>/<task>, the id the plan's own dependency graph spells a node with. Absent for every launch that named none, which is the common case and every spec written before the field. The shape here is task.PlanTaskProblem's, applied by the launcher on write and by task.Parse on read: two or more '/'-separated elements, each starting with a letter or a digit and otherwise letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 128 bytes. Two rules of that one the pattern cannot carry are that a '.' or '..' element and a control character are refused. It is a display-only join hint: nothing authorises, admits or budgets anything by it. Needs a 0.11.2 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's planTaskSince): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it.

external.description: The ticket this run's work item came from outside Fugaro with (task.Spec.External, the orchestrator's WorkItem.external): github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>, one issue, lower-case as the installation's own App answers a repository name. Absent for every task whose item carries no external id, which is every launch before this field and every item nobody ingested. The pattern is internal/orchestrator's externalRE, the rule that admitted the id when the daemon's state was written and read it back: no flag writes this field, so the launcher copies an id the state already validated rather than applying a second rule of its own. It is what the run's pull request names so a merge closes that issue (Fixes #<n> in the run's own repository, Fixes <owner>/<repo>#<n> in another): a reference, never text the run follows. Needs a 0.26.0 runner, which is why the daemon's launcher drops it against an older job image (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's externalSince and externalSkew) rather than writing a task that run dies on at bootstrap, task.Parse decoding with DisallowUnknownFields.

author.description: Who the launch says its commits are authored by (D604), written into the agent's git environment as GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL. The launcher is what fills the field (A2b), and only for a repository that opted in by writing git.author: launcher (D606): the address is the local config's commit_email when it is set, else the launcher's own identity Me (the user: key, else git config user.email), and the name is commit_name, else git's user.name, else the address's local part. A commit_email that is neither the address the launcher launches as nor a forge noreply address is refused at the launch (D649). It is omitted, so the run's own identity authors its commits, for a review or artifact launch — neither pushes, so an identity there would be a claim about commits never made (D605) — for a launcher whose identity is no address (user: alice, a CI box, a bot account) and against a job image not shown to read the field (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's authorSkew drops it and says so). It is a claim, not a proof, and the runner enforces nothing beyond its shape (task.AuthorProblem). A task that carries one needs a runner that reads the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without the author — which is why the launch drops the field there instead of writing a task such a run dies on.

name.description: The author's name, as git writes it into the commit header. At most task.MaxAuthorNameLen runes, one line, with no control character and no angle bracket: it becomes a git header value, and a newline in it would forge the rest of the header block.

email.description: The author's address, as git writes it into the commit header and as a forge maps it to an account. At most task.MaxAuthorEmailLen runes (RFC 5321's maximum path length), one address: exactly one '@' with a local part before it and a domain after it, no control character and no angle bracket.

resumes.description: The run whose pause this one picks up (task.Spec.Resumes, runstore.PauseMemberResumes, docs/model-credentials-routing): the run that suspended itself on this pull request, whose pause.json names the stage it was in, the session it saved and the commit it pushed, and where this run enters rather than at the first stage (R18, D3185). Written only by the orchestrator's launcher, and only for a pause the credentials service recorded (R19, D3189). A resumed run is a follow-up of the run it continues, so branch, pr and previous_run are required beside it and name the same run: the chain link carries the chain's remaining budget (D1045 to D1047), the pull request's branch holds the checkpoint, and a task naming one run for the chain and another for the pause is refused by task.Spec.Validate. Needs a runner that reads the member: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than starting the work at its first stage.

owner_ruled.description: The repository owner's ruling this follow-up was launched with (OD1, fugaro run --owner-ruled): their answer to the findings a run on this pull request left for them, which no code change could settle. The runner appends it to the follow-up's brief verbatim and echoes it onto the run's record (runstore.Record.OwnerRuled). Bounded at task.MaxOwnerRuledBytes, never blank, and carrying no control character other than a newline or a tab — the rules task.Spec.Validate applies. A launcher refuses a follow-up on a pull request whose last run stopped waiting on owner decisions unless this carries one, so the loop that spent the runs in the first place cannot start again.

review_prs.description: Set only for a mode: review recipe (design generic-tool §3.6): the pull requests to review, 1 to 4, never together with branch/pr/previous_run.

context_repos.description: The repositories this run reads and never writes (fugaro run --context, plan task C5a; D613): owner/name, one to five, each admitted by the project's published allow_repos. They are recorded on the task and in the launcher-minted claim of the run's own identity (fcr), whose reader the credentials service is: the service cannot read the task, and the task file is writable by the job. Absent for every launch that named none, which is the common case and every spec written before the field. The shape is task.ContextReposProblem's, applied by the launcher on write and by task.Parse on read: each entry must look like owner/name, which is task.CanonicalRepo's own rule — two or more '/'-separated elements of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', with no '.' or '..' element (the part the pattern cannot carry). Needs a 0.26.0 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's contextReposSince): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it.

change_set.description: The change set this run is a member of (fugaro run --change-set, plan task D1; reconciliation-image-setup D613 step 2, D616, D642): the set's ID and the whole member list, which the one launch that created every member run wrote into each member's task. Membership is fixed there and read from here — the settle step acts only when every member lists the same set — so a task that names a set is a member of it and nothing else can make it one. Absent for every launch that named no change set, which is every spec written before this field. The shape is task.Spec.Validate's, applied by the launcher on write and by task.Parse on read: two to five members, the ID naming the first member's run, each member a canonical owner/name (task.CanonicalRepo's rule, the part the pattern cannot carry being the '.' and '..' elements) with a run ID, no repository twice, and this run's own repository among them. The repository-uniqueness, first-member-id and own-repository rules are task's and not this document's: a JSON Schema cannot compare one property across items. Needs a 0.27.0 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's changeSetSince) and refused until the settle step ships (D616): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the member as an ordinary run whose pull request nothing would settle.

mutate.description: The mutation check the launch asked for (fugaro review --mutate <file:test>, docs/cloud-senior-review D885): the file in the reviewed head the runner flips a boolean literal in, and the test that must kill it. At most one, and only for a review of exactly one pull request — the rules the `dependentRequired` and `allOf` entries below carry, and the ones task.Spec.Validate applies: the check runs the head's own code in a subprocess of the review job's own (D891(a)), and one worktree holds the whole review only when one pull request was resolved. task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so a runner before the release that reads this field refuses the whole spec. No launch writes the field yet: the command that would is CSR2's and the launcher-side gate it needs (the `…Since` constant internal/cli/recipes_skew.go declares) is CSR6's, so the gate lands with the flag rather than the launch being left for the job to refuse. Needs a 0.16.0 runner.

file.description: Go source inside the reviewed worktree, spelled relative and slash-separated. The pattern is the ask's own shape — no leading slash, no empty segment, a .go suffix — and what confines the path to the worktree is the runner's own read through an os.Root with an Lstat in front of it: that refuses a symlink rather than following it, and a path with a "." or ".." segment never reaches it (internal/runner's mutationFile).

test.description: The Go test that must fail once the mutant is applied. The runner quotes it before handing it to `go test -run`, so this is the ask's own shape rather than the only thing between a name and that flag.

follow_up_of.description: The run a triage follow-up was filed from (docs/post-review-triage, task.Spec.FollowUpOf; decision D1843): the parent run's ID and the keys of the deferred findings the task was filed for. The CLI writes it out of the parent's own record, since a job writes only its result record and never files a follow-up; no run reads it, and it is what tells work a run left behind from work somebody asked for. Absent for every task that is not one of those, which is every task written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. A task that carries it needs a runner that knows the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without its parent, which is why the launcher gates a launch that would set it (the launcher-side gate T-TR10 of that plan adds).

run.description: The parent's run ID, of the one shape every run ID has (task.ValidRunID), which task.Spec.Validate applies: a follow-up whose parent is not a run ID names nothing a reader could find the deferred findings in.

keys.description: The parent record's own finding keys (D1850, a hash of a file and a summary) that this task carries: one task per group, and the ungrouped case is one key. A task the CLI files always names at least one, since a group is formed from the deferrals themselves, but neither this schema nor task.Spec.Validate requires it: a key is only ever compared with the keys the parent's record carries, and never joined into a path, a command or a prompt. Unlike the spec's other lists, this one is carried through as written — the keys are opaque hashes, not launcher text.

importance.description: How much this follow-up matters (task.FollowUpOf.Importance, docs/outer-loop-escalation, D2040): the launcher orders the important ones ahead of new work and notifies about them, and that is the whole of what the mark decides — an important follow-up is not an approved one (G6, F21). It is written from the merge judge's classification when a judge ran and from a deterministic rule when none did (a security or data-loss class, or impact 5, is important), so task.Spec.Validate refuses a value outside the two names rather than reading it as a third opinion about a finding. Absent — and so empty — for every follow-up filed before this field, including every one filed by hand, and empty is not `minor`: it is no answer, and a reader that has to sort one applies its own rule rather than reading a mark nobody wrote. It is a new key inside an existing block, so an older runner that knows `follow_up_of` still refuses the whole spec on it (task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields), and the launcher gates it with `model_grade`'s constant (taskGradeSince, internal/cli/recipes_skew.go), which covers both fields of this release.

debt.description: True marks a task filed from a triage deferral (task.Spec.Debt, docs/post-review-triage), which is what `fugaro runs ls --debt` lists. Absent — and so false — for every task that is not one, which is every task written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. Like `follow_up_of` it needs a runner that knows it (task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields), which is why a launch that writes it is to be gated the same way (the launcher-side gate T-TR10 of that plan adds).

security.description: The launch's own request that this run's review be the strongest one it can be (task.Spec.Security, docs/security-classification, D1517): `fugaro run --security` writes it, and a task may say it by hand. It is raise-only — true turns review level 3 on whatever paths the run changed, and false changes nothing, since there is no value that asks for less — so it needs no fence and no allow-list, exactly as --mode's own raise needs neither. The project layer's security.always_level_3 (schemas/project-layer.schema.json) makes the same request for every run of the project, and the repository's own security: rows escalate a matching diff independently of either. Absent — and so false — for every task that did not ask, which is every task written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. Like the spec's other new fields it needs a runner that knows it (task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields), so a launch that writes it is refused on a job image older than the release whose runner reads it (securityRequestSince, internal/cli/recipes_skew.go).

model_grade.description: The model grade this run runs at (task.Spec.ModelGrade, docs/outer-loop-escalation, D2039's E4): which of the project layer's two grades the run's coder — and its judge, which runs the coder's model — runs on, and whose credential or pool their calls go out on. A task names a grade and never a model or a credential (G11): the project layer's `defaults.model_grades` (schemas/project-layer.schema.json, published on the policy node) is what says which model and which credential each name resolves to, and the runner resolves it at bootstrap (internal/runner's applyGrade). A grade the project sets nothing for refuses the run there rather than falling back to a model nobody chose, which is D2039's reading: the plan ships no default for either grade. The two names are escalation.Grades' and the field is closed to them, so a model ID or a credential name here is refused by task.Spec.Validate and by this schema both. Absent — and so empty — for every task that names no grade, which is every task written before this field and every launch the ladder did not escalate, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. Like the spec's other new fields it needs a runner that knows it (task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields), so a launch that writes it is refused on a job image older than the release whose runner reads it (taskGradeSince, internal/cli/recipes_skew.go).

mode.description: The resolved recipe's mode, written by the launching CLI ("artifact" and "evaluate" today; an implement or review recipe writes nothing, so those specs are unchanged). The runner selects the run's shape from it at bootstrap, before the recipe is resolved, and cross-checks it against the resolved recipe afterwards. Needs a 0.8.0 runner, which is why an artifact launch at a job image older than that is refused at launch; "evaluate" is the judge run's mode (docs/model-ab-testing A5.2) and needs the runner that carries it.

review_class.description: task.Spec.ReviewClass, the marker the cloud tier of `fugaro troubleshoot` writes (docs/troubleshoot-cloud D2411): it admits a run to the review-only job variant, whose container mounts no App key and no Claude token, without the run being a review — the tier's recipe is mode: artifact (D2402) while the job it must run on is that variant (D2403). It is legal only beside mode: artifact (Spec.Validate refuses it in every other mode, and task.Parse does too), and it never overrides the mode: a mode: review spec is a review whatever this property says. Absent for every launch that is not a diagnosis, so every other spec is byte-identical to what the previous release wrote. Needs the runner of the release that first carries the diagnose step, which is why the launcher gates a launch that sets it at the job image the way it gates the step kind itself: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task as an ordinary artifact run.

rigor.description: The rigor mode the launching CLI asked for (fugaro run --mode, docs/rigor-modes implementation-plan T1.6): the run's own request, which may raise the mode its layers resolve and never lower it (D6). Absent asks for none, which is every launch without the flag, and the run then resolves from fugaro.yaml's rigor block and the project layer alone. It is not `mode` above: that one is the recipe's mode, a different question with a different vocabulary. Needs a 0.11.1 runner, which is why a launch that would set it at an older job image is refused at launch.

paths.description: The paths the launching CLI declared this run will touch (fugaro run --path, repeatable), in the order --path named them: the runner matches them against the base branch's rigor.areas rules at D22's first moment, and a path matching no rule changes nothing. Absent for every launch that declared none. A blank path is no path (the same rule as task.InputNameBlank's, expressed as the pattern), and both bounds are task.MaxDeclaredPaths and task.MaxDeclaredPathBytes. Needs a 0.11.1 runner, the same gate `rigor` above has.

promote.description: The area a promote run raises (fugaro run --promote, docs/rigor-modes/levels-spec.md §4, LD6, docs/rigor-modes/levels-reconciliation.md §3b item 12): the area's name and this repository's paths in it, which the launcher resolved out of the repository's own fugaro.yaml (rigor.areas) before the task was stored. The run reads that area's backlog items and its code, works at the level `rigor` above names, and closes the items its own diff pays down (D31). `paths` above carries the same paths, since the area's own rule is what the run's level resolves from. Absent for every launch that is not a promote run, so every other spec is byte-identical to what the previous release wrote. Needs the runner that reads it: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec, and the launch is refused at the job image the way `rigor` and `paths` above are.

tier.description: The expectation tier of this run (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, plan T8.1): what the run is expected to cost and take, which selects one tier of fugaro.yaml's governance.tiers. Absent is untiered — every spec written before this release, and every launch that declares no tier. fugaro run --tier writes it, and a --pr follow-up carries the tier the run it follows recorded (plan T8.1b). The vocabulary is internal/tier's and spelled exactly as it spells it: a near miss ("Trivial", "SMALL") is refused, never read as an unknown tier. It is not `rigor` above: that one is the review's depth, a different question with a different vocabulary. Needs a 0.13.0 runner: an older runner's task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields and refuses the field outright.

expected_scope.description: Roughly which files or areas the run is expected to touch (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3's expectation envelope). It is paths and never prose: nothing here reaches a prompt. Absent for every spec that declares none, and unlike `tier` above no launcher writes it yet. A blank entry is no path (the same rule as task.InputNameBlank's, expressed as the pattern), and both bounds are task.MaxDeclaredPaths and task.MaxDeclaredPathBytes. Needs a 0.13.0 runner, the same as `tier` above.

inputs.description: The files the launching CLI attached (fugaro run --attach, docs/artifact-runs/spec.md §4), in the order --attach named them: each one is stored under runs/<slug>/<run>/inputs/<name> and downloaded by a mode: artifact run into <checkout>/inputs/. Absent for every launch that attached nothing. The name's own shape is checked where it becomes a filesystem path (the launcher's, then the runner's), never here. Needs a 0.8.0 runner, which is why an --attach launch at an older job image is refused at launch.

name.description: The name the file is stored and written under. A name of nothing but whitespace is no name, the same rule task.InputNameBlank applies before the launcher uploads anything.

sha256.description: The sha256 the launcher read while uploading the file. The runner verifies the object it downloads against it, so a mismatch leaves nothing at the destination.

reports.description: The project's stored reports the launching CLI handed this run (fugaro run --commit-reports, plan task R16, D2754), in the order the launcher read them: each one is stored under runs/<slug>/<run>/reports/<name>, where <name> is the report's name in the mirror (<slug>/<YYYY>/<key>.md for a repository's report, <YYYY>/<key>.md for the project's aggregate), and the commit_reports step downloads it, verifies it against the size and the sha256 here, and commits it into the checkout's mirror folder. Absent for every launch that handed none in, and for every run whose recipe has no commit_reports step. The name's own shape is checked where it becomes a path in the repository (the commit step, through digest.ParseMirrorPath), never here. Needs a 0.27.0 runner: an older runner's task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields and refuses the field outright, which is why a --commit-reports launch at an older job image is refused at launch.

name.description: The report's mirror-relative name, which is also the object's leaf under the run's reports/ prefix. A name of nothing but whitespace is no name, the same rule task.InputNameBlank applies in Spec.Validate.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes the launcher uploaded, hashed in the same pass that wrote them. The runner verifies each downloaded object against it and against its size, so a mismatch leaves nothing at the destination.

recipe.description: The recipe the launching CLI resolved; absent means, for a first run, agent.recipe in fugaro.yaml at the ref, else default; for a follow-up, default (docs/recipes/spec.md).

name.description: The recipe the launcher resolved: a recipe name, or the name of the project's copy of one (recipe.IsNameOrCopy) — the copy a migrated repository's runs embed.

project_layer.description: The project layer the launching CLI read (docs/layered-config/spec.md §8); the runner resolves fugaro.yaml against it. Absent: none. Needs a 0.6.0 runner.

oauth_token.description: The named Claude OAuth account this run holds (docs/named-oauth-tokens/spec.md): the account an agent.auth: oauth workflow used, and, for a mixed agent.auth: api-key run, the one Claude account its review and adversarial stages are served by beside the provider key the gateway holds (docs/mixed-credentials/spec.md §11) — either way it names the job variant the run is on. Absent, or "default" itself, name the repository's unnamed claude-oauth-token secret; "default" is therefore never a value here, which is why the pattern alone (matching "default") is not enough. The not clause's second name is bitbucket-token, the one name the credentials bundle reserves for the platform's own git credential: both it and "default" pass the pattern and the length cap, so the not clause is the only rule that refuses them, and task.Spec.Validate refuses them in the same words (config.ReservedClaudeAccountName). maxLength is required alongside the pattern: each of the pattern's {0,30} repetitions may consume one character or, via the dash alternative, two ("-" plus the alphanumeric it must precede), so the pattern alone admits names up to 61 characters (e.g. "a" + 30 repetitions of "-a") — config.MaxClaudeAccountNameLen (internal/config/claude_accounts.go) is 31, and this must match it exactly. The anyOf's second and third branches are the account axis's non-account values (config.AnthropicKeyAccount and config.ProviderKeyAccount, docs/api-key-review D1417 and AK6a): the sentinels the project's own Anthropic API key and the project's provider key are named by, outside the pattern by construction, and a review launch writes one here as the run's own credential — so each is written as its own alternative rather than by widening the pattern, and each literal is pinned to the Go constant by schemas' own test.

compression_off.description: task.Spec.CompressionOff, written by fugaro run --no-compression: it disables agent.compression for this run only, overriding the repository's own reviewed choice (docs/headroom-compression/spec.md §4). There is no field and no flag to force compression on, so this is the only direction the override goes. Needs a 0.12.0 runner, which is why the launcher gates at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's compressionSince) every launch whose task carries it: one that writes it, which --no-compression does only when the resolved configuration turns compression on, and a --pr follow-up or a --retry, which inherits it from the run it continues and so carries it even after the repository's key has been removed. task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it.

digest_runs.description: The report run's manifest (task-governance plan T3.6, task.Spec.DigestRuns): the run IDs of the records the digest step may read, which the launching CLI listed from this repository's own runs/ prefix — the last 40 days, newest first, at most task.MaxDigestRuns of them. Absent for every launch that is not a report run, so a spec written for one is byte-identical to what the previous release wrote. The job reads each named record by name and never lists, so this list is what decides which records a run reads; the runner still refuses an ID outside its own repository's prefix (G2). It is accepted only with a recipe whose first step is digest (task.RecipeUsesDigest), the only step that reads it; a repository-sourced recipe carries its name alone, so the launcher judges the file it resolved (internal/cli/run_digest_manifest.go) and the runner resolves that name at the task's ref. Needs a 0.13.0 runner (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's digestSince, the same gate the digest step itself needs): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without its manifest. The launcher's image gate refuses at an older job image every launch whose task carries this field, whatever its recipe's source (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's recipeSinceFor reads the manifest before the recipe), and one whose task carries the catalog run-digest's own text; a repository report recipe whose listing came out empty carries neither, and there the older runner refuses the digest step at bootstrap.

ab.description: The A/B pair block of a sampled launch (docs/model-ab-testing, decisions D550-D573; task.AB): which pair this run belongs to, which arm it is, and, for a challenger, the coder model it runs and the fact that it never publishes. Absent for every launch that was not sampled — which is every launch today, since nothing samples yet — so a spec without it is byte-identical to what the release before this field wrote. Both arms of one pair carry the same pair_id and differ in nothing but this block (D555): the challenger travels here and never in overrides.model, which a run with no per-role models applies to every stage and would move the reviewer both arms share, which is why an ab block and overrides.model never appear together. The vocabulary is closed, like rigor's and tier's: an unknown arm, publish, challenger_source or slot is refused rather than read as something else. `slot` (D728, docs/review-levels-ab-jobmax B1.1) says which one thing the pair varies: a coder pair — the slot an absent key means — holds every reviewer fixed, and a pair at a review slot holds the coder fixed and carries its challenger's champion_run, the run whose recorded patch that challenger's reviewer replays (B1.2). Needs a runner that knows these fields: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running a challenger as a publishing run, and the launcher's own gates are what keep a sampled launch, or one at a review slot, off such a job (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's slotSince).

pair_id.description: The pair both arms belong to: one value, written by the launcher onto both tasks, so a reader joins the two records by it. Opaque to the runner, and a blank one names no pair (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule, as the paths entries below carry it).

arm.description: Which arm this run is. The champion is the run the developer gets and publishes exactly as an unsampled run; the challenger is a shadow (task.ABArmChampion, task.ABArmChallenger).

publish.description: Present only on a challenger, and only as "none" (task.ABPublishNone): the challenger's arm never pushes, opens, updates or comments on a pull request, and the safety switch is stated rather than left to an absent field (D554). A champion publishes as it always did and carries nothing here.

challenger.description: The coder model the challenger arm runs, and the one difference between the arms (D555). It is an entry of the project layer's own challenger list, which the runner re-checks at bootstrap rather than trusting this text, so this schema does not carry that list's shape. A blank one is no model (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule).

challenger_source.description: Who named the challenger: the owner, in the project layer, never the repository's own file (D556, task.ABChallengerOwner). It is the seam D572 reserves for a later auto-flip writer; nothing reads it to pick a challenger.

slot.description: The one thing the pair varies (D728, task.ABSlot): coder is the pair A1.1 already writes — a second full run on another coder model, with every reviewer held fixed, which is D555 as it stands — and l1, l2 and l3 are the review slots, whose challenger replays that level's review over the champion's own recorded patch instead of running a coding loop (B1.2). Absent means coder (task.AB.EffectiveSlot): every block written before this key is a coder pair, so the empty spelling cannot be read as a pair nobody could score. Both arms of a pair carry the same slot — it says what the pair varies, not what this arm does — and a champion carries it as readily as a challenger.

champion_run.description: The champion's run ID, present only on a challenger whose slot is a review slot (task.AB.ChampionRun, D728, B1.2): it names the run whose recorded patch, runs/<repo-slug>/<run-id>/ab/patch.diff, this arm's reviewer reads, which is what makes the two arms of a review pair judge the same code. Absent on a champion — which is the run its own block names — and on a coder pair's challenger, which runs the whole task itself; task.Spec.Validate and the if/then below refuse it there rather than ignoring it, and the pattern is run_id's own form (task.ValidRunID), because a blank or invented ID would send the replay looking for an object nobody wrote.

review_levels.description: What the launch asks each review level to do (docs/review-levels-ab-jobmax, D724; config.ReviewLevels, read by task.Spec.ReviewLevels): l1 is the first line of review, l2 the senior round and l3 the adversarial one, and each holds the model that runs it, the effort it runs at, whether it runs at all, and what it is asked to focus on. Absent for every launch that asks nothing about levels, which is every launch today: no launcher writes the field until L1.2's --review-levels and its version gate land, so a spec without it is byte-identical to what the release before this field wrote. Written by fugaro run (L1.2); agent.levels in fugaro.yaml carries the same block (L1.3), and both are held to one set of rules (config.ReviewLevels.Validate). Needs a runner that knows the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task with the levels it was given.

review_spec.description: The spec a launched review is checked against (task.Spec.ReviewSpec, docs/review-against-task R2): the task the pull request was written for, the follow-up's own text beside it, and the plan task whose section of its plan the reviewer is also pointed at. The launcher writes it for `fugaro review` and for `fugaro run --recipe review-only`, which resolve it through one shared resolver (D2934), and the review job's runner reads it and reads no other run; an in-run review carries no block, since its runner holds the run's own task already. It is DATA and never an instruction (R3): the reviewer compares the diff against it, and the runner quotes it redacted, cleaned and nonce-fenced under a sentence that says so. It is never the pull request body, which whoever can edit the pull request can rewrite (spec §2), and never a source the review job fetches itself: the launcher hands the bytes in (F3). Absent for every launch that is not a launched review, which is every spec written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. The rules here are task.ReviewSpecProblem's, applied by the launcher on write and by task.Parse on read: a source from the closed vocabulary, a run source naming the root run's ID, a file source carrying no run id, and a none source with a reason and without text. The trim task.Validate applies to the reason is not expressible here, so a reason of nothing but whitespace passes this document and is refused by the decoder.

source.description: Where the spec came from (task.ReviewSpecSource): `run` is a pull request a Fugaro run produced, whose spec is the root run's stored task the launcher read out of the runs bucket; `file` is a spec a person handed in with `fugaro review --spec FILE`; `none` is no spec at all, and `reason` says why. Required whenever the block is present, which is what makes a review_spec that names no source a document neither reader accepts.

reason.description: Why there is no spec, and it belongs to `source: none` alone — the rules in the `allOf` below require it there (task.ReviewSpecProblem). The values a launcher writes are `--code-only`, `no run found`, `pick of different tasks` and `own-step recipe` (R2, F35). The pattern is the rule the paths entries carry: at least one non-whitespace character, so a reason of nothing but spaces is no reason.

run.description: The root run's ID, present when `source` is `run` and refused beside `file`: it names the run whose stored task `text` holds, so a reader can say which record the review was judged against (R16). The pattern is run_id's own form (task.ValidRunID). It is the launcher's claim and not a proof — an earlier run of the same repository can rewrite that record — which is the residual the owner accepted (O3).

text.description: The spec itself: the root task's text, or the text of a `--spec FILE`. Bounded by task.MaxReviewSpecBytes (R4's 16 KiB), and refused beside `source: none` by the `allOf` below. maxLength counts characters while the decoder's cap counts bytes, so this schema is the looser of the two for text outside ASCII, exactly as the level focus below records. The launcher clips a longer root task at a line with a note naming what was dropped, as clipBaseInstructions does, so a spec it writes never exceeds what the decoder accepts; a `--spec FILE` over the cap is refused at launch with its size.

followup.description: The latest follow-up run's own text, added beside `text` so a pull request a follow-up wrote is judged against what it was for and not only against the fix instructions (spec §2, R1). Absent when the pull request has no follow-up, and bounded by task.MaxReviewSpecBytes like `text`.

plan_task.description: The plan task copied off the root task (task.Spec.PlanTask, D2932): when it is set, the reviewer is also pointed at that task's section of its implementation plan. It is a copy and not a second claim — nothing joins it into a path — and its shape here is task.PlanTaskProblem's, the same rule the top-level `plan_task` above carries, applied by task.Parse on read. Absent when the root task named no plan task.

from_findings.description: True marks a follow-up launched from a review's own findings (`fugaro run --pr N --review-run R`, task.Spec.FromFindings, R2/F30): such a run's task text is the rendered findings followed by the person's TEXT, and only the person's part is a brief — the rest is a reviewer's words, and quoting them as the spec would make a reviewer the author of the brief the next review judges against (F25). Absent — and so false — for every other launch, which is every spec written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's.

own_text.description: The person's own words on a findings follow-up (task.Spec.OwnText, R2): the TEXT they typed, kept apart from the findings the task text opens with, so a review of that pull request quotes what the person asked for and leaves the reviewer's words out (R1). Absent for every other launch, which is every spec written before this field, so such a spec is byte-identical to the previous release's. Bounded by task.MaxReviewSpecBytes, and the `dependentRequired` entry below refuses it beside no `from_findings`: a launch that did not mark the findings has no person's text to keep apart from them. That entry fires on the key being present while the decoder fires on it being non-empty, so a hand-written `own_text: ""` is refused here and accepted there; no launcher writes one, its own field being omitempty.

level.description: One review level's settings (config.LevelSetting). The keys are the Go field names except `none`, which is config.LevelSetting.Off: `none` is what an owner or a launcher writes to say a level does not run, where `off: true` would read as a value rather than as a level's absence. Three of the decoder's rules are not expressible here, and are refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate instead: an effort outside `effort`'s five values (config.Efforts; Claude Code itself warns and sends the model's default for the flag, and drops the environment variable and the settings key in silence, so nothing downstream refuses one), a focus carrying a control character, a bidi or zero-width one, a line or paragraph separator, or invalid UTF-8 (the project layer's own rule for a value out of a file, internal/config's badRune, which is why the pattern here cannot carry it), and `none: true` — or the level's model named `none` (config.NoneModel), which is the same switch written the other way — beside any other key, which is refused rather than read — a level that is off has no settings. The bound is a byte count while maxLength counts characters, so this schema is the looser of the two for text outside ASCII: a focus of 500 ASCII characters is at both caps, and one of 500 characters outside ASCII is over the decoder's and under this one's.

model.description: The exact model ID this level runs (config.LevelSetting.Model). The literal `none` is not an ID: it is the level's own switch written the other way (config.NoneModel), so `model: none` is exactly `none: true`: the level does not run, the settings beside it are refused, and the string never resolves as a model name. Absent leaves the level on the model its own layer resolves — agent.models.reviewer for a senior level — and it is bounded by allowed_models as every other model setting is, which the runner checks rather than this schema.

effort.description: The reasoning effort this level runs at (config.LevelSetting.Effort, config.Efforts): the five values the pinned Claude Code accepts, from the least to the most, as measured against Claude Code 2.1.283 (docs/multi-model.md). Absent asks for none, which is the model's own default — that is not the same as "auto" or "unset", which are not values here. The vocabulary is closed in both directions: a value outside it is refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate, because Claude Code would take it without a word.

none.description: True turns this level off (config.LevelSetting.Off): the level's step is not run, and the three settings beside it are refused rather than read; a level whose `model` is the literal `none` (config.NoneModel) is the same switch written the other way, which the decoder folds into this key rather than reading as a model name. False, and an absent key, both mean the level runs. A level that is off under the owner's floor is refused at launch (L3.1, L1.4), which is not this schema's rule: nothing here reads the floor.

focus.description: What this level's reviewer is asked to look at, in the launcher's own words (config.LevelSetting.Focus). It is data and never a command: the runner puts it in the reviewer's prompt as quoted text, and it is never put through a shell or joined into a path. 500 is config.MaxLevelFocusBytes, which the decoder applies as a byte count as well.
